title: Rivalry Without the Scoreboard: Why Royal Challengers Bengaluru Fixtures Feel Personal
dek: Some fixtures feel personal before a ball is bowled. For Royal Challengers Bengaluru, the most frequent opponent is Kolkata Knight Riders, and the history between them explains some of the edge.
excerpt: Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Kolkata Knight Riders have met more than any other pairing in Royal Challengers Bengaluru's history. The record between them, its streaks and its close finishes, is what gives the fixture its weight.

sections.heading: Why Some Fixtures Feel Personal
body: Rivalries are built from history: repeated meetings, memorable finishes, streaks that one side's fans never let the other forget.
The CricField warehouse holds no survey, sentiment or social-media data, so it cannot measure what fans feel. It can measure what they have watched.

sections.heading: Recent Memory
body: Fans weight recent results most heavily. RCB have won {{ev:rv-last}} of the last five meetings.

sections.heading: Most-Played Is a Stand-In
body: The most frequent opponent is a measurable stand-in for a rivalry. The rivalry fans feel most may be with a different side, shaped by geography, a final or a single incident.
Identifying that would need fan survey data.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: History Gives the Fixture Its Edge
body: Royal Challengers Bengaluru's record against Kolkata Knight Riders has enough streaks and close finishes to explain why the fixture matters.
What it means to fans is a question the scoreboard cannot answer.
